policy_facts: The one change to what's sent widens the 18 November entry. An answer an earlier version kept about what made a Lovejoin box, without the keys that transaction spent, is now asked about once more wherever it says a deposit made the box, whatever accounts the wallet knows. Today's wording says 'only where the wallet knows an account that answer may not have been checked against', which becomes false for deposits and needs rewording. The request is the same as before: on mainnet the data layer's pool listing usually answers with no request; on preprod, or when the data layer can't answer, Koios tx_info. Until it's answered, the box is held and Mix my boxes again waits.

Nothing new is sent to tell the wallet's own Lovejoin deposits from someone else's. The wallet checks the keys a deposit's transaction spent, already kept since the gap-g6#2 change, against your public accounts' keys and your private sessions' one-time account keys. Those are every session the wallet knows of, and 20 past the last, derived on your device, asking no one.

What's kept: one new sealed count, per Lovejoin pool, of the boxes someone else (or another device) put in under your key (`someoneElse`, beside `unsure` in the encrypted Lovejoin record). It's derived from what's already kept, for Home. Nothing else new is kept.

A box someone else put in under your key, brought back by hand, is recorded in the encrypted Seedelf history as money received, not as a box back from Lovejoin. Coin selection then treats it as a payment from whoever put it in.

Behaviour the policy may want to state: Mix my boxes again leaves out a box someone else (or another device) put in under your key. Pay from my private balance anyway still takes it, after a warning that this ties the mix, and the private UTxOs it spends, to whoever put it in.

New pub struct KoiosScript {hash, size, type, bytes} (:72). script_ref (:412) writes [kind, script]: kind 0 with a native script's CBOR as it is, or 1-3 with Plutus bytes as a byte string. It refuses a script that can't be written: no bytes, not hex, a size or hash that disagrees, an unknown type, or a native script that isn't one CBOR item within MAX_DEPTH (core's non-recursive within_depth). utxo_cbor (:341) writes the map form with key 3 = #6.24(bytes) whenever there's a script, a datum hash beside it as [0, hash]; rows without a script are encoded as before. The own-output push is at :1525. output_parts itself is unchanged: its typed outputs lose a native script's original bytes. policy_facts: gap-g1#2 needs a dated Changes entry and the Effective date; fold it into the 18 November entry if it ships in 1.9.2. When you sign a site's transaction that pays your own Seedelf, from the account sites use or from a private session, the wallet keeps a note of it in the sealed Seedelf history on your device. The note holds the transaction ID, which of its outputs are yours, and which public account or private session signed. Once a balance reading finds the payment, the note becomes its history entry: 'Made private', or 'Back from a private session'. A note whose transaction never lands is deleted after 30 days, and at most 50 are kept. Nothing is sent to anyone for it. It's written before the site gets the signature, because the site may send the transaction itself. The policy row 'Your contacts, your Seedelf history, …' could name it.

gap-g9#1 (for G8 to decide; the decision said no policy entry for gap-g9#1, and this cache is my addition). While the wallet is unlocked on mainnet, it keeps in session storage, cleared on lock, which transactions spent its own private UTxOs, as the data layer's private index reports to everyone. The newest 100 are kept, in the existing `seedelf.contract.<network>` view. It uses them to list money that the same phrase sent from another browser profile or device as 'Already in your private balance', carrying the history of what that spend took, instead of 'Received'. No new request is made. Through Koios or on preprod there's no spender, so such money still reads as received; privacy.md:177 says so.

gap-g1#1 changes nothing the wallet sends or keeps. Only the on-device classes, the selection order (G1a's Purpose::Mint) and the words change: a copy of a register the wallet already holds is never counted as received, and a stealth mint or a pool's start takes a box back from Lovejoin that pays alone before received money. privacy.md says it. items.left: The owner's steps, in order: (1) Settings → Environments → New environment 'release'. (2) Add yourself as required reviewer and leave 'Prevent self-review' off, since you push the tag and approve the run. (3) Deployment branches and tags → Selected branches and tags → add a Tag rule '*.*.*'. (4) Add RELEASE_GPG_KEY and GPG_PASSPHRASE as environment secrets, from your own copy (GitHub won't show the repository secrets' values). (5) Delete the repository secrets RELEASE_GPG_KEY and GPG_PASSPHRASE. (6) Merge, then tag the CLI patch release only on a commit that has the new release.yml, and approve sign-and-publish when the three builds pass. What breaks if the order is wrong: 5 before 4 means the import refuses the empty key, nothing is signed or published, and 'Re-run failed jobs' works once the secrets are in place. A tag before 1-3 lets GitHub create an empty 'release' environment at the first run (from GitHub's docs, not checked live), and the job signs at once with the repository secrets, unguarded as today; nothing fails, and that environment is then configured. A tag on a commit without the new release.yml (e.g. cut from cli/stranger-rows without main) after 5 runs the old layout, which signs in its build jobs with the deleted repository secrets: every build fails at its import and nothing is published; before 5, it runs as today, unprotected. A tag rule that doesn't match, or 'protected branches' left on, makes the environment refuse the job: nothing is published, so fix the rule and re-run. 'Prevent self-review' on, with you as the only reviewer, means you can't approve and the run waits until it times out (30 days). Keeping the repository secrets after 4 still works (environment secrets win), but any job on any branch that names them can still read the key. Not run: a live gpg import and signature with a throwaway key; the Bash guard refuses commands that name a GPG home. A hosted run wasn't possible either.
